subject: Performance / SLO qualification & benchmark methodology - follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@edgefin.tech>, Linda Park <linda.park@edgefin.tech>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 10 Jul 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap & next steps - performance / SLO qualification

Thanks again for taking the time today - good conversation. Quick recap and next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Goal: validate Redwood's ability to meet EdgeFin's production SLOs for the new real-time summarization feature (P95 latency, throughput, concurrency, streaming behavior).
- Requirements you flagged on the call: P95 end-to-end latency target ~300ms for streaming responses at expected batch sizes, baseline throughput ~500 QPS sustained with spiky bursts to 2k QPS, ability to handle 200 concurrent active streams with KV-cache reuse.
- We proposed running a reproducible benchmark using our public harness plus your canonical prompt sets and production-like traffic profiles.

As agreed, we need the following from your side to start the benchmark: 
1) The canonical prompt set (representative 50-200 prompts or a sampling strategy if the dataset is larger).
2) Measurement definitions - what counts as success for streaming (first-byte latency vs final token completion), how you want percentiles reported (p50/p95/p99), and any tail trimming rules.
3) A privacy-safe sample traffic shape: expected QPS distribution over a 24-hour window, and typical concurrency levels.

I'm attaching our benchmark harness (redwood-benchmark-harness-v1.zip) and a short plan template (edgefin-benchmark-plan.xlsx) to make it easier - please drop your prompt set and measurement definitions in the plan and share back.

Next steps / owners: 
- Samir / Linda: share prompt set + measurement defs in the plan by EOD Tuesday (July 13).
- Redwood (Rishi / Dev): validate harness compatibility, propose test config and resource estimate by Thursday (July 15).
- Run initial reproducibility pass and share results + raw logs by Monday (July 19).

If any of the targets above are incorrect or you want to prioritize different metrics (e.g., cold-start latency for new sessions), flag that in your reply.

Thanks - talk soon.

-- 
Marissa Cole

Redwood Inference

From: Samir Shah <samir@edgefin.tech>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Linda Park <linda.park@edgefin.tech>
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps - performance / SLO qualification

Marissa - really appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Latency: our production SLA for this feature is p95 <= 300ms for perceived streaming responsiveness (we measure from first-streamed token to first user-visible token for interactive flows; we also track final token completion but that's a secondary metric).
- Throughput & concurrency: target sustained throughput 500 QPS across our EU + US traffic (we can shard tests regionally if useful). Peak bursts up to 2k QPS expected for short periods. Concurrency target: 200 active concurrent streaming sessions.
- Streaming specifics: we prefer server-initiated chunking with initial partial result within 100-150ms when possible. For fairness, we can provide a small set of prompts that exercise different output lengths (short/medium/long).
- Measurement: please report p50/p95/p99 for first-byte (initial chunk) and time-to-last-token; include CPU/GPU utilization, memory, and KV cache hit rates.

We'll upload the prompt set and the measurement tab in the plan spreadsheet by Tuesday morning (July 13). I’ll also include two synthetic traffic traces that approximate our peak and off-peak shapes.

Thanks - Samir
Samir Shah
Director of Engineering, EdgeFin
samir@edgefin.tech

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@edgefin.tech>, Linda Park <linda.park@edgefin.tech>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 11 Jul 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps - performance / SLO qualification

Perfect - that aligns with what we discussed. A couple notes on the benchmark methodology from our side to keep results reproducible and comparable: 

- Harness versioning: we'll run tests with the attached harness v1 and record checksums + environment snapshot (GPU type, driver, CUDA, runtime flags).
- Prompt sampling: if you provide a larger corpus, we'll run stratified sampling by length and token-complexity to ensure coverage. Please mark any prompts that include PII so we can omit or synthetic-substitute.
- Measurement definitions:
  * first-byte latency = time from request accept to first token emitted
  * time-to-last-token = end-to-end latency for full generation
  * KV-cache hit rate measured as ratio of tokens served from warmed cache vs cold
  * tail reporting: p50/p95/p99 (no tail trimming unless you explicitly request)
- Reproducibility: we'll publish the test harness config (seed values, traffic profile JSON) and attach raw logs + pprof traces where possible.

Rishi / Dev - once Samir uploads the plan, can you review the harness compatibility and propose: 1) a recommended cluster config (GPU type + count), 2) batch/concurrency knobs, 3) estimated run time + cost for a 1-hour representative run? If you can also note any limitations for streaming-first-byte measurement (we may need a small custom probe), include that in the response.

Samir - thanks for the traffic traces and prompt sets in advance. We'll aim for an initial reproducibility pass Monday (July 19) as proposed and will surface any measurement gaps earlier if they come up.

Best,
Marissa

--

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Internal: EdgeFin benchmark plan - action items

Internal note / action items (copy of external thread for context):

EdgeFin will provide: prompt set (50-200 samples), two synthetic traffic traces (peak/off-peak), and explicit measurement definitions (first-byte vs final-token). Targets: p95 <= 300ms first-byte for streaming, sustained 500 QPS, 200 concurrent streams, bursts to 2k QPS.

Please prepare the following by Thursday (July 15):
- Rishi: recommended cluster config (GPU SKU + cluster size), batching strategy, expected concurrency handling. Include notes on how we will measure first-byte streaming latency accurately (do we need a client-side probe or server-side timestamping?).
- Dev: validate harness v1 against our current runtime (include script to capture first-byte time and to dump KV-cache hit-rate metrics). Produce a runbook for reproducibility (env variables, seed values, driver versions).
- Include rough cost estimate (cloud GPU hours) and ETA for a 1-hour run producing p50/p95/p99 for both first-byte and time-to-last-token.

I've attached the harness + plan in the external thread (redwood-benchmark-harness-v1.zip / edgefin-benchmark-plan.xlsx).

Thanks - Marissa

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Shah <samir@edgefin.tech>
Date: Mon, 12 Jul 2027 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Internal: EdgeFin benchmark plan - action items

Acknowledged - quick notes / proposal: 

1) Recommended test config (initial pass):
   - GPU: 8x A100-80GB (or equivalent), single-shot cluster for regional test (US).
   - Model variant: quantized 8-bit candidate + fp16 baseline for head-to-head.
   - Batch strategy: dynamic batching with max batch 16 and target latency budget per batch of 80ms for first-byte.

2) Measurement probes:
   - First-byte: add client-side probe that records request-send timestamp and first-chunk-received timestamp; also instrument server to emit first-token server timestamp in header for cross-checks.
   - Time-to-last-token: measured on client side; collect reconstruction of token timing from server logs for verification.

3) KV-cache: warm cache by replaying 10k representative requests before measurement window; report hit rate every 5 minutes.

4) Run plan / cost & ETA:
   - 1-hour representative run (mix of short/medium/long prompts, 500 QPS sustained) - estimated 4 GPU-hours on 8x A100 cluster (~32 GPU-hours total due to multi-run baseline + ablation) - rough cloud cost estimate: $6k- $9k depending on spot pricing.
   - We can reduce to smaller config (4x A100) for an initial smoke test to validate measurement plumbing (~1-2k cost).

5) Reproducibility & artifacts:
   - Produce harness config JSON, hash of all artifacts, raw logs, and a summary CSV with p50/p95/p99 for first-byte and time-to-last-token.

Next steps: Dev, can you validate the harness against our runtime this afternoon and confirm ability to capture first-byte timing? I’ll prepare a short README for the measurement definitions and add a section on known caveats (e.g., network noise, client variance).

- Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
